name: rggen
desc: Code generation tool for control and status registers
why: Generates hardware control and status register code from specs, a door into how chip register maps are made.

brief.what_it_is: RgGen is a command-line code generator for chip register maps (CSRs). You describe registers and bit fields in a human-readable spec (Ruby API, YAML, JSON, TOML, XLSX/ODS/CSV spreadsheets, or SystemRDL with a plugin), and it writes SystemVerilog RTL, a UVM register model (uvm_reg/RAL), a C header, and Markdown documentation. Verilog, Veryl, and VHDL RTL need extra plugins. A browser-based Web UI at rggen.github.io/rggen-webui does the same job without installing anything.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as automation for ASIC, IP, FPGA, and RTL engineers, who otherwise hand-write the same register logic, UVM models, and software headers from one register map.
brief.how_it_works: The core tool reads the register map spec and a configuration file, then runs output writers for each target: SystemVerilog and the bus protocols (AMBA APB, AMBA AXI4-Lite, Avalon-MM, Wishbone), UVM RAL, C header, and Markdown. Other languages and input formats come in as plugins (rggen-verilog, rggen-veryl, rggen-vhdl, rggen-systemrdl), and the README says plugins can also add custom bit field types and host bus protocols. The README does not describe the internal pipeline in more detail.

commands_seen.context: Installs RgGen and its Ruby dependencies into the system gem root (the README's default route).
Homebrew route on macOS or Linux; also pulls in Ruby if needed and the VHDL, Verilog, and Veryl plugins.

commands_seen.cmd: docker run -ti --rm -v ${PWD}:/work --user $(id -u):$(id -g) rggendev/rggen-docker:latest -c config.yml -o out block_0.yml
commands_seen.context: Runs RgGen from the rggen-docker image, mounting the current directory as /work and writing output to out.
Main example from the sample repo: -c gives the configuration file, -o gives the output directory, and the last argument is the register map spec.

commands_seen.cmd: rggen -c config.yml --plugin rggen-verilog --plugin rggen-veryl --plugin rggen-vhdl uart_csr.yml
commands_seen.context: Runs RgGen with the three RTL plugins loaded through --plugin.
Installs into a custom directory instead of the system root.
Points Ruby at the custom gem directory; the README also says to add $GEM_PATH/bin to PATH.

brief.install_notes: Needs Ruby 3.2 or later, installed first (the README links to the Ruby install page). Homebrew installs Ruby itself if needed. For a custom install location, set GEM_PATH and PATH as shown. If you have RgGen older than 0.9, gem install may fail with an executable conflict; the README points to a wiki page for three fixes. Verilog, Veryl, VHDL, and SystemRDL need their plugin gems installed and passed with --plugin. Docker is an alternative that avoids the Ruby setup. The sample config and UART register map are in the rggen-sample repository.
brief.standout: One spec, many outputs: a single register map feeds SystemVerilog, Verilog, Veryl, VHDL, UVM, C, and Markdown, and the input can be a spreadsheet, which many chip teams already use. The plugin system lets teams add their own bit field types and bus protocols, and an in-browser UI removes the install step entirely.
brief.status: unknown for release and commit dates: I did not see a release date or last-commit date in the README. Signs of active work: a 2026 copyright line, a CI badge, a Discord and mailing list, and a September 2026 DVCon Japan publication listed. Treat as actively developed, but verify the repo's recent activity yourself.
brief.caveats: Verilog RTL under Verilator needs the -Wno-unoptflat switch. Icarus Verilog handles Verilog RTL only. Verilog, Veryl, VHDL, and SystemRDL output each need a separate plugin gem. Requires Ruby 3.2+. Upgrading from pre-0.9 versions can hit an executable name conflict. The README has a few typos and a Veryl plugin link that looks mistyped ('rggen-very' in the Homebrew section). The README links to a wiki for usage and plugin docs, which I did not read. The homepage itself is a JavaScript app and returned no readable text to me.
quotes: RgGen is a code generation tool for ASIC/IP/FPGA/RTL engineers.
No installation required — RgGen runs entirely in the browser.
Feedbacks, bug reports, questions and etc. are wellcome!
